SUMMARY:
The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary special local regulation (SLR) for the navigable waters of the Atlantic Ocean surrounding the Key West Main Shipping Channel and the waters between Sunset Key and Wisteria Island. This action is necessary to provide for the safety of life on these navigable waters near Key West, FL during the Race World Offshore World Championship 2026 event beginning on November 4, 2026, and ending on November 8, 2026. This regulation prohibits persons and vessels from entering the regulated area unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port Key West or their designated representative.
DATES:
This rule is effective from 9:00 a.m. on November 4, 2026, through 6 p.m. on November 8, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
To view available documents go to
https://www.regulations.gov
and search for USCG-2026-1264.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
If you have questions about this rule, contact MSTC Mathew Mason, Sector Key West Waterways Management Division, U.S. Coast Guard; telephone 305-292-8823, or email
Mathew.R.Mason@uscg.mil
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
I. Table of Abbreviations
CFR Code of Federal Regulations
COTP Captain of the Port
DHS Department of Homeland Security
FR Federal Register
NPRM Notice of proposed rulemaking
§ Section
SLR Special Local Regulation
U.S.C. United States Code
II. Background and Authority
On August 5, 2026, an organization notified the Coast Guard that they will sponsor a high-speed powerboat race. The Coast Guard received a request under 33 CFR 100.15 from the Race World Offshore Organization for a Marine Event Permit to host a high-speed powerboat race within the Key West Main Shipping Channel. The event will be held from 9:00 a.m. until 6:00 p.m. on November 4, 6, and 8, 2026, in Key West, FL. The races will include approximately 80 participants and 300 spectator craft.
The Captain of the Port Key West (COTP) is issuing this special local regulation (SLR) under the authority in
46 U.S.C. 70041
. The COTP has determined that potential hazards associated with the operation of vessels at high speeds include the possibility of collision within the navigable channel, as well as the possibility that participants operating within approaches to local public and private boat facilities might collide with or otherwise interfere with boaters near those facilities. The purpose of this rulemaking is to protect event participants, spectators, and transiting vessels before, during, and after the scheduled event.
Because of these potential hazards, the Coast Guard is issuing this rule without prior notice and comment. As is authorized by
5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B)
, the Coast Guard finds that good cause exists for not publishing a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) with respect to this rule because it is impracticable and contrary to the public interest. The Coast Guard was notified of the final details of the event concerning spectator locations and confirming event boundaries until October 29, 2026, but we must establish this SLR by November 4, 2026, to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment. Therefore, we do not have enough time to solicit and respond to comments.
For the same reasons, the Coast Guard finds that under
5 U.S.C. 553(d)(3)
, good cause exists for making this rule effective less than 30 days after publication in the
Federal Register
.
III. Discussion of the Rule
This rule establishes a temporary SLR from 9:00 a.m. until 6:00 p.m. on November 4, 6, and 8, 2026. The special local regulation will cover all navigable waters within 800 feet of the Racecourse and the navigable waters extending outward 300 feet from the North shoreline of Sunset Key. No vessel or person will be permitted to enter the regulated area without obtaining permission from the COTP or their designated representative.
IV. Regulatory Analyses
We developed this rule after considering numerous statutes and Executive orders related to rulemaking. Below we summarize our analyses based on a number of these statutes and Executive orders.
A. Impact on Small Entities
The regulatory flexibility analysis provisions of the Regulatory Flexibility Act of 1980,
5 U.S.C. 601-612
, do not apply to rules that are not subject to notice and comment. Because the Coast Guard has, for good cause, waived the notice and comment requirement that would otherwise apply to this rulemaking, the Regulatory Flexibility Act's flexibility analysis provisions do not apply here.
Under section 213(a) of the Small Business Regulatory Enforcement Fairness Act of 1996 (
Pub. L. 104-121
), if this rule will affect your small business, organization, or governmental jurisdiction and you have questions, contact the person listed in the
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT
section. Small businesses may send comments to the Small Business and Agriculture Regulatory Enforcement Ombudsman and the Regional Small Business Regulatory Fairness Boards by calling 1-888-REG-FAIR (1-888-734-3247). The Coast Guard will not retaliate against small entities that question or complain about this rule or any policy or action of the Coast Guard.
B. Collection of Information
This rule will not call for a new collection of information under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (
44 U.S.C. 3501-3520
).
C. Federalism and Indian Tribal Governments
We have analyzed this rule under
Executive Order 13132
, Federalism, and have determined that it is consistent with the fundamental federalism principles and preemption requirements described in that Order.
Also, this rule does not have tribal implications under
Executive Order 13175
, Consultation and Coordination with Indian Tribal Governments, because it does not have a substantial direct effect on one or more Indian tribes, on the relationship between the Federal Government and Indian tribes, or on the distribution of power and responsibilities between the Federal Government and Indian tribes.
D. Unfunded Mandates Reform Act
As required by The Unfunded Mandates Reform Act of 1995 (
2 U.S.C. 1531-1538
), the Coast Guard certifies that this rule will not result in an annual expenditure of $100,000,000 or more (adjusted for inflation) by a State, local, or tribal government, in the aggregate, or by the private sector.
E. Environment
We have analyzed this rule under Department of Homeland Security Directive 023-01, Rev. 1, associated implementing instructions, and Environmental Planning COMDTINST 5090.1 (series), which guide the Coast Guard in complying with the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (
42 U.S.C. 4321
et seq.
), and have determined that this action is one of a category of actions that do not individually or cumulatively have a significant effect on the human environment.
(
printed page 69503)
This rule is a special local regulation. It is categorically excluded from further review under paragraph L61 of Appendix A, Table 1 of DHS Instruction Manual 023-01-001-01, Rev. 1.

33 CFR part 100
as follows:
PART 100—SAFETY OF LIFE ON NAVIGABLE WATERS

.
2.
Add 100.T07-1264 to read as follows:
§ 100.T07-1264
Special Local Regulation; Main Shipping Channel, Key West, FL.
(a)
Location.
This special local regulation applies to the following regulated areas: all navigable waters extending 800 feet outward from the racecourse beginning at a point latitude 24°33′20.78″ N, longitude 81°48′45.47″ W thence to latitude 24°33′53.93″ N, longitude 81°48′21.10″ W then to latitude 24°33′54.41″ N, longitude 81°48′28.99″ W thence to latitude 24°32′36.89″ N, longitude 81°49′46.61″ W thence to latitude 24°32′33.32″ N, longitude 81°49′41.06″ W thence to latitude 24°32′27.38″ N, longitude 81°49′02.40″ W thence to latitude 24°32′27.38″ N, longitude 81°48′59.90″ W thence returning to the point of origin at latitude 24°33′20.78″ N, longitude 81°48′45.47″ W. All navigable waters extending 300 feet outward from the North shoreline of Sunset Key. These coordinates are based on the 1984 World Geodetic System (WGS 84).
(b)
Definitions.
As used in this section,
designated representative
means a Coast Guard Patrol Commander, including a Coast Guard coxswain, petty officer, or other officer operating a Coast Guard vessel and a Federal, State, and local officer designated by or assisting the Captain of the Port Sector Key West (COTP) in the enforcement of the regulated area.
Participant
means all persons and vessels registered with the event sponsor as a participant in the race.
(c)
Regulations.
(1) All non-participants are prohibited from entering, transiting through, anchoring in, or remaining within the regulated area described in paragraph (a) of this section unless authorized by the COTP or their designated representative.
(2) To seek permission to enter, contact the COTP or the COTP's representative on VHF-FM channel 16. Those in the regulated area must comply with all lawful orders or directions given to them by the COTP or the COTP's designated representative.
(d)
Enforcement period.
This section will be enforced from 9:00 a.m. until 6:00 p.m. on November 4, 6, and 8, 2026.

Title:
Organic Handler Market Promotion Assessment Exemption under Federal Marketing Orders.
OMB Number:
0581-0216.
Expiration Date of Approval:
April 30, 2027.
Type of Request:
Extension of a currently approved information collection.
Abstract:
The information collection requirements in this request are essential to carry out the intent of the Agricultural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937, as amended (
7 U.S.C. 601-674
) (the Act), to provide respondents the type of service they request and to administer several Federal marketing orders. Marketing order regulations help ensure adequate supplies of high-quality product and adequate returns to producers. The Secretary of Agriculture is authorized to oversee marketing order operations and issue regulations recommended by a board or committee of representatives from each commodity industry.
The information collection requirements in this request are essential to carry out the intent of the Act, to provide the respondents the type of service they request, and to administer the marketing order programs. Under the Act, marketing orders may authorize: production and marketing research, including paid advertising; volume regulation; reserves, including pools and producer allotments; container requirements; and quality control. Assessments are levied on handlers regulated under the marketing orders.
On May 13, 2002, the Farm Security and Rural Investment Act (
7 U.S.C. 7901
) amended the Federal Agriculture Improvement and Reform Act of 1996 (
7 U.S.C. 7201
), exempting any person who handles or markets solely 100 percent organic products from paying these assessments with respect to any agricultural commodity that is produced on a certified organic farm, as defined in the Organic Foods Production Act of 1990 (
7 U.S.C. 6502
). A certified organic handler can apply for this exemption by completing a “Certified Organic Handler Application for Exemption from Market Promotion Assessments Paid Under Federal Marketing Orders,” and submitting it to the applicable marketing order board or committee.
Section 900.700 (
7 CFR part 900
) provides for exemption from assessments. This notice applies to the following marketing orders:
7 CFR parts 906
(Texas citrus), 915 (Florida avocados), 923 (Washington cherries), 925 (California desert grapes), 927 (Oregon/Washington Pears), 930 (Tart cherries grown in seven states), 932 (California olives), 948 (Colorado potatoes), 955 (Vidalia onions), 956 (Walla Walla onions), 958 (Idaho/Oregon onions), 959 (South Texas onions), 966 (Florida tomatoes), 981 (California almonds), 982 (Oregon/Washington hazelnuts), 984 (California walnuts); 985 (Northwest spearmint oil), 986 (Pecans grown in 15 states), 987 (California dates), 989 (California raisins), and 993 (California dried prunes). Currently, handling requirements for Marketing Order 993 (California dried prunes) are suspended at the industry's request until July 30, 2030 (
89 FR 13587
). While its reporting requirements are suspended and currently inactive, it is included in this renewal period of this information collection package until the industry decides whether to proceed with marketing order termination in 2030.
The information collected is used only by authorized representatives of the USDA, including the AMS Specialty Crops Program's regional and headquarters' staff, and authorized employees of the boards or committees. Authorized board or committee employees are the primary users of the information and AMS is the secondary user.
Estimate of Burden:
Public reporting burden for this collection of information is estimated to average 0.25 hours per response.
Respondents:
Eligible certified organic handlers.

210.
Estimated Total of Annual Responses:
210.
Estimated Number of Responses per Respondent:
1.
(
printed page 69524)
Estimated Total Annual Burden on Respondents:
52.5 hours.
Comments are invited on:
(1) Whether this collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the agency, including whether the information has practical utility; (2) the accuracy of the agency's estimate of the burden of the collection of information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used; (3) ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information collected; and (4) ways to minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who respond, including through the use of appropriate automated, electronic, mechanical, or other technological collection techniques or other forms of information technology.
All responses to this notice will be summarized and included in the request for OMB approval. All comments will also become a matter of public record.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
The United States Department of Energy (DOE) regulates electricity exports from the United States to foreign countries in accordance with section 202(e) of the Federal Power Act (FPA) (
16 U.S.C. 824a(e)
) and regulations thereunder (
10 CFR 205.300
). Sections 301(b) and 402(f) of the DOE Organization Act (
42 U.S.C. 7151(b)
and
7172(f)
) transferred this regulatory authority, previously exercised by the now-defunct Federal Power Commission, to DOE.
Section 202(e) of the FPA provides that an entity which seeks to export electricity must obtain an order from DOE authorizing that export (
16 U.S.C. 824a(e)
). On January 8, 2026, the authority to issue such orders was delegated to the DOE's Assistant Secretary for the Office of Electricity by Redelegation Order No. S3-DEL-OE1-2026.
On September 1, 2026, TPS filed an application (Application or App.) with DOE for renewal of export authority to transmit electric energy from the United States to Mexico for an additional five-year term. App. at 2. TPS was granted export authorization under Order No. EA-431-A on March 4, 2022, which expires on March 4, 2027.
According to the Application, TPS is a Nebraska corporation that is authorized to do business in the States of Nebraska, Alabama, Illinois, Texas, New York, Ohio, Oklahoma, California, Delaware, Nevada, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Washington. TPS is an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Tenaska Energy Inc. (Tenaska), which is “an independent developer and owner of power production facilities located throughout the United States.”
Id.
at 3. TPS is a “power marketer authorized by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to make sales of electric power at wholesale in interstate commerce at market-based rates.”
Id.
In addition, TPS states that it “does not currently own or control electric generation or transmission facilities, and does not have a power supply of its own in the United States that would cause its electricity exports to have a reliability, fuel use, or system stability impact” and that it will “purchase the electricity that it may export, on either a firm or an interruptible basis, from wholesale generators, electric utilities, federal power marketing agencies and affiliates through negotiated agreements that have been voluntarily executed by the selling parties after considering their own need for any such electricity.”
Id.
at 4. Thus, “TPS's proposed electricity exports will not impair or tend to impede the sufficiency of electric power supplies in the United States or the regional coordination of electric utility planning or operations.”
Id.
at 4-5.
(
printed page 69554)
The Applicant also states that it will “make all necessary commercial arrangements and will obtain any and all other regulatory approvals required in order to carry out any electricity exports” and that it “agrees to abide by the export limits contained in the relevant export authorization of any transmission facilities over which TPS exports electricity to Mexico.”
Id.
at 5.
The existing international transmission facilities to be utilized by the Applicant have been previously authorized by Presidential permits issued pursuant to
Executive Order 10485
, as amended, and are appropriate for open access transmission by third parties.
See
App. at Exhibit A.

Any person desiring to be heard in this proceeding should file a comment to the Application at

Comments concerning TPS's Application should be clearly marked with OE Docket No. EA-431-B. Comments will be posted along with the relevant application on the program website at

or by emailing
Electricity.Exports@hq.doe.gov

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Authority for This Rulemaking
The FAA's authority to issue rules regarding aviation safety is found in Title 49 of the United States Code. Subtitle I, Section 106 describes the authority of the FAA Administrator. Subtitle VII, Aviation Programs, describes in more detail the scope of the agency's authority. This rulemaking is promulgated under the authority described in Subtitle VII, Part A, Subpart I, Section 40103. Under that section, the FAA is charged with prescribing regulations to assign the use of the airspace necessary to ensure the safety of aircraft and the efficient use of airspace. This regulation is within the scope of that authority as it would amend the route structure to maintain the efficient flow of air traffic within the National Airspace System (NAS).
Comments Invited
The FAA invites interested persons to participate in this rulemaking by submitting written comments, data, or views. Comments are specifically invited on the overall regulatory, aeronautical, economic, environmental, and energy-related aspects of the proposal. The most helpful comments reference a specific portion of the proposal, explain the reason for any recommended change, and include supporting data. To ensure the docket does not contain duplicate comments, commenters should submit only one time if comments are filed electronically, or commenters should send only one copy of written comments if comments are filed in writing.
The FAA will file in the docket all comments it receives, as well as a report summarizing each substantive public contact with FAA personnel concerning this proposed rulemaking. Before acting on this proposal, the FAA will consider all comments it receives on or before the closing date for comments. The FAA will consider comments filed after the comment period has closed if it is possible to do so without incurring expense or delay. The FAA may change this proposal in light of the comments it receives.
Privacy:
In accordance with
5 U.S.C. 553(c)
, DOT solicits comments from the public to better inform its rulemaking process. DOT posts these comments, without edit, including any personal information the commenter provides, to
www.regulations.gov
,
as described in the system of records notice (DOT/ALL-14 FDMS), which can be reviewed at
www.dot.gov/​privacy
.

An electronic copy of this document may be downloaded through the internet at
www.regulations.gov
.
Recently published rulemaking documents can also be accessed through the FAA's web page at
www.faa.gov/​air_​traffic/​publications/​airspace_​amendments/​
.
You may review the public docket containing the proposal, any comments received and any final disposition in person in the Dockets Operations office (see
ADDRESSES
section for address, phone number, and hours of operations). An informal docket may also be examined during normal business hours at the office of the Eastern Service Center, Federal Aviation Administration, Room 210, 1701 Columbia Avenue, College Park, GA 30337.
Incorporation by Reference
Domestic VOR Federal Airways are published in paragraph 6010(a) of FAA Order JO 7400.11, Airspace Designations and Reporting Points, which is incorporated by reference in
14 CFR 71.1
on an annual basis. This document proposes to amend the current version of that order, FAA Order JO 7400.11M, dated July 30, 2026, and effective September 15, 2026. These updates would be published in the next update to FAA Order JO 7400.11. FAA Order JO 7400.11M, which lists Class A, B, C, D, and E airspace areas, air traffic service routes, and reporting points, is publicly available as listed in the
ADDRESSES
section of this document.
Background
The FAA is planning to decommission the Andrews, MD (ADW), VORTAC on August 5, 2027. The FAA determined the Andrews VORTAC should be decommissioned to reduce the dependency on ground-based navigation facilities and legacy en-route structure as the NAS continues to transition to a more efficient Performance Based Navigation (PBN) route structure. The Air Traffic Service (ATS) routes affected by the planned navigational aid (NAVAID) decommissioning are VOR Federal Airways V-44, V-170, and V-312. With
(
printed page 69510)
the planned decommissioning of the Andrews VORTAC, the remaining ground-based NAVAID coverage in the area is insufficient to enable the continuity of the affected ATS routes. This lack of continuity necessitates the proposed amendments to V-44, V-170, and V-312 by removing portions of the airways that would lack coverage.
To overcome the proposed modifications to the affected routes, instrument flight rules (IFR) traffic could use adjacent VOR Federal Airways V-33, V-93, V-123, V-166, V-268, V-378, V-379, and V-499 or receive air traffic control (ATC) radar vectors to fly through or circumnavigate the affected area. Additionally, IFR pilots with Area Navigation (RNAV)-equipped aircraft could also use the adjacent RNAV Routes T-224, T-287, T-291, T-295, T-307, T-315, T-320, T-335, T-356, T-358, T-447, and T-476 or navigate point-to-point using the existing waypoints that will remain in place to support continued operations through the affected area. Visual flight rules (VFR) pilots who elect to navigate via airways through the affected area could also take advantage of the ATC services listed previously.
The Proposal
The FAA is proposing an amendment to
14 CFR part 71
that would modify domestic VOR Federal Airways V-44, V-170, and V-312 to support the planned decommissioning of the Andrews VORTAC.
V-44:
V-44 currently extends between the Columbia, MO (COU), VOR/Distance Measuring Equipment (VOR/DME) and the Centralia, IL (ENL), VORTAC; and between the Parkersburg, WV (JPU), VOR/DME and the Albany, NY (ALB), VORTAC. The airspace below 2,000 feet mean sea level (MSL) outside the United States is excluded.
The FAA proposes to remove the segment of the airway that extends between the Martinsburg, WV (MRB), VORTAC and the intersection of the Baltimore, MD (BAL), VORTAC 122° and Sea Isle, NJ (SIE), VORTAC 267° radials due to the planned decommissioning of the Andrews VORTAC. As amended, the airway would extend between the Columbia, MO (COU), VOR/DME and the Centralia VORTAC; between the Parkersburg VOR/DME and the Martinsburg VORTAC; and between the Sea Isle VORTAC and the Albany VORTAC. The airspace below 2,000 feet MSL outside the United States is excluded.
V-170:
V-170 currently extends between the Jamestown, ND (JMS), VOR/DME and the Badger, WI (BAE), VOR/DME; and between the Slate Run, PA (SLT), VORTAC and the intersection of the Andrews VORTAC 060° and Baltimore VORTAC 165° radials. The airspace within R-5802 is excluded when R-5802 is active.
The FAA proposes to remove the segment of the airway that extends between the intersection of the Dupont, DE (DQO), VORTAC 223° and the Andrews VORTAC 060° radials; and the intersection Andrews VORTAC 060° and Baltimore VORTAC 165° radials due to the planned decommissioning of the Andrews VORTAC. As amended, the airway would extend between the Jamestown, ND (JMS), VOR/DME and the Badger VOR/DME; and between the Slate Run VORTAC and the Dupont VORTAC. The airspace within R-5802 is excluded when R-5802 is active.
V-312:
V-312 currently extends between the intersection of the Andrews VORTAC 060° and Baltimore VORTAC 165° radials and the intersection of the Coyle, NJ (CYN), VORTAC 090° and Kennedy, NY (JFK), VOR/DME 154° radials. The airspace within R-5002D is excluded when R-5002D is active, and the airspace below 2,000 feet MSL outside the United States is excluded.
The FAA proposes to remove the segment of the airway that extends between the intersection of the Andrews VORTAC 060° and Baltimore VORTAC 165° radials and the intersection of the Andrews VORTAC 060° and Woodstown, NJ (ODD), VORTAC 230° radials. As amended, the airway would extend between the Woodstown VORTAC and the intersection of the Coyle VORTAC 090° and Kennedy VOR/DME 154° radials. The airspace within R-5002D is excluded when R-5002 is active, and the airspace below 2,000 feet MSL outside the United States is excluded.
The full proposed descriptions of the above routes are set forth below in the proposed text amendments to part 71. The NAVAID radials listed in the VOR Federal airway description regulatory text of this NPRM are stated in degrees True north.
Regulatory Notices and Analyses
The FAA has determined that this proposed regulation only involves an established body of technical regulations for which frequent and routine amendments are necessary to keep them operationally current. It, therefore: (1) is not a “significant regulatory action” under
Executive Order 12866
; (2) is not a “significant rule” under DOT Order 2100.6B, “Policies and Procedures for Rulemakings” (March 10, 2025); and (3) is expected to result in, at most, de minimis costs from compliance with applicable operating requirements or minor flight rerouting for operators choosing to navigate around the controlled airspace. Since these proposed amendments are routine and the expected impact to operators is de minimis, the FAA certifies that this proposed rule, when promulgated, will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities under the criteria of the Regulatory Flexibility Act.
Environmental Review
This proposal will be subject to an environmental analysis in accordance with FAA Order 1050.1G, “
FAA National Environmental Policy Act Implementing Procedures
” prior to any FAA final regulatory action.

AGENCY:
Department of Commerce (Department).
ACTION:
Final rule.
SUMMARY:
The Department is effectuating nomenclature changes throughout
Title 15 of the Code of Federal Regulations
to remove all references to an outdated official title (“Assistant General Counsel for Employment, Litigation and Information”) and replace them with updated references to the appropriate official (the “Assistant General Counsel for Litigation and Strategic Support” or the “Assistant General Counsel for Information Security and Emerging Technologies”). This action is necessary to reflect the current structure and roles within the Department and to ensure that the regulations at Title 15 remain up to date and refer the public to the appropriate officials. This action is intended to promote clarity and efficiency without making any substantive changes to any regulations.
DATES:
The rule is effective November 4, 2026.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Daniel Sweeney, Deputy General Counsel for Economic, Statistical, and Regulatory Affairs, Office of the General Counsel, at (240) 474-3619.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
As part of a restructuring of the Department's Office of the General Counsel, the official role of “Assistant General Counsel for Employment, Litigation and Information” has been eliminated. However, that title remains referenced in
15 CFR part 2
(§§ 2.4(b), 2.5(a)-(b));
15 CFR part 4
(§§ 4.10(b)(1), 4.10(c), 4.23(d)(2), 4.25(a)(2), 4.25(g)(3)(ii), 4.28(a)(1)(ii), 4.28(a)(2)(ii)(D), 4.29(b)(1), 4.29(c), 4.29(e), 4.29(g)(1), 4.29(h), 4.29(i), and Appendix B); and
15 CFR part 15
(§§ 15.13(b)(1), 15.13(c), 15.13(d)(1), and 15.17). This action effectuates a nomenclature change and replaces those references with updated references to the appropriate officials—specifically, the “Assistant General Counsel for Litigation and Strategic Support” for parts 2 and 15, and the “Assistant General Counsel for Information Security and Emerging Technologies” for part 4. This action also updates the room number for the Assistant General Counsel for Information Security and Emerging Technologies. This action does not make any other changes to the Code of Federal Regulations and does not make any substantive changes. This action ensures that the Department's regulations remain up to date and reduces the risk of confusion and/or administrative delay.
Regulatory Classifications
A. Administrative Procedure Act
Pursuant to
5 U.S.C. 553(a)(2)
, the provisions of the Administrative Procedure Act requiring notice of proposed rulemaking and the opportunity for public participation are inapplicable to this rule because it relates to “agency management or personnel or to public property, loans, grants, or contracts.” This rule only updates references to the titles of appropriate Department officials and thus falls squarely within the ambit of “agency management or personnel.” Accordingly, the Department issues this final rule without prior public notice and comment or a delayed effective date under
5 U.S.C. 553(a)(2)
.
B. Executive Orders 12866, 14192, and 13132
The Office of Management and Budget has determined this rule is not significant pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 12866. This rule is not subject to E.O.14192 because this rule is not significant. This rule does not contain policies having federalism implications as the term is defined in
E.O. 13132
.
C. Regulatory Flexibility Act
Because a notice of proposed rulemaking and an opportunity for public participation are not required to be given for this rule by
5 U.S.C. 553(a)(2)
, the analytical requirements of the Regulatory Flexibility Act (
5 U.S.C. 601
et seq.
) are not applicable. Accordingly, no regulatory flexibility analysis is required, and none has been prepared.
D. Paperwork Reduction Act
This rule will not impose additional reporting or recordkeeping requirements under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995,
44 U.S.C. 3501
,
et seq.

[Office of Management and Budget #: 0970-0171]
AGENCY:
Office of Child Support Enforcement, Administration for Children and Families, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.
ACTION:
Request for public comments.
SUMMARY:
The Office of Child Support Enforcement (OCSE), Administration for Children and Families (ACF), U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, is requesting a 3-year extension of the Voluntary Acknowledgment of Paternity and Required Data Elements for Paternity Establishment Affidavits. No changes are proposed to the data elements, but burden has been adjusted to reflect improved automation for processes.
DATES:
Comments due December 4, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
The public may view and comment on this information collection request at:
https://www.reginfo.gov/​public/​do/​PRAViewICR?​ref_​nbr=​202610-0970-006
.
You can also obtain copies of the proposed collection of information by emailing
infocollection@acf.hhs.gov
.
Identify all emailed requests by the title of the information collection.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Description:
Section 466(a)(5)(C) of the Social Security Act requires states to enact laws ensuring a simple civil process for voluntarily acknowledging paternity via an affidavit. The development and use of an affidavit for the voluntary acknowledgment of paternity would include the minimum requirements of the affidavit specified by the Secretary under section 452(a)(7) of the Social Security Act and give full faith and credit to such an affidavit signed in any other state according to its procedures. The state must provide that, before a mother and putative father can sign a voluntary acknowledgment of paternity, the mother and putative father must be given notice, orally, or through the use of video equipment, and in writing, of the alternatives to, the legal consequences of, and the rights (including any rights, if one parent is a minor, due to minority status) and responsibilities of acknowledging paternity. The affidavits will be used by hospitals, birth record agencies, and other entities participating in the voluntary paternity establishment program to collect information from the parents of nonmarital children.
Respondents:
The parents of nonmarital children, state and tribal agencies operating child support programs under Title IV-D of the Social Security Act, hospitals, birth record agencies, and other entities participating in the voluntary paternity establishment program.
Annual Burden Estimates
Annual burden estimates have been updated to remove ordering brochures from the annual burden hours calculation, as ordering brochures is not required under federal guidelines. With advancements in automation and digital service delivery, most partners now rely on electronic devices located in hospitals and other automated public-facing platforms to deliver education on paternity establishment and highlight the benefits of signing the paternity establishment affidavit. This results in a 40 percent overall decrease in estimated annual burden compared to the most recently approved annual burden estimates (2024). The number of responses and estimated time per response for the remaining instruments have not changed.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106788; File No. SR-CboeEDGX-2026-073]
October 30, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 21, 2026, Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc. (“Exchange” or “EDGX”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Exchange filed the proposal as a “non-controversial” proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
3
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
4
]
The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “EDGX Options”) proposes to introduce enhancements to the Missed Liquidity Report offered as part of the Cboe Timestamping Service.
The text of the proposed rule change is also available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
), the Exchange's website (
https://www.cboe.com/​us/​equities/​regulation/​rule_​filings/​edgx/​
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes introduce enhancements to the Cboe Timestamping Service, which is a market data service comprised of the Missed Liquidity Report, Missed Cancels Report and All Cancels Report. Specifically, the Exchange seeks to update the Missed Liquidity Report to now include Complex Order Auction (“COA”)
[
5
]
and Complex Automated Improvement Mechanism (“C-AIM”)
[
6
]
(
printed page 69602)
events (collectively, “Auction Orders” or an “Auction”), as well as a new price field that, for records related to Auction Orders, includes each price of the subscribing Member's orders, modify messages, and quotes, as well as each price level at which options orders were executed during an Auction. The Exchange is not proposing any enhancements to either the Missed Cancels Report or the All Cancels Report.
[
7
]
Background
Currently, the Cboe Timestamping Service provides timestamp information for orders, quotes and cancels for market participants. More specifically, the Cboe Timestamping Service reports provide various timestamps relating to the message lifecycle throughout the Exchange System.
[
8
]
The reports are optional products that are available to all Members and Members may opt to choose any combination of reports or no reports at all. Corresponding fees are assessed based on the number of reports selected.
[
9
]
Notably, the data included in these reports is based only on the data of the market participant that opts to subscribe to the reports (“Recipient Member”) and does not include information related to any Member other than the Recipient Member. The Exchange restricts all other market participants from receiving another market participant's data. Additionally, no report includes real-time market data. Rather, the reports contain only historical data from the prior trading day and are only available after the end of the trading day, generally on a T+1 basis.
Specifically, the Missed Liquidity Report provides time details for executions of orders and quotes that rest on the EDGX Book
[
10
]
where the Member receiving the report attempted to execute against that resting order within an Exchange-determined amount of time (not to exceed 1 millisecond) after receipt of the first attempt to execute against the resting order or quote and within an Exchange-determined amount of time (not to exceed 100 microseconds) before receipt of the first attempt to execute against the resting order or quote.
[
11
]
For example, if a Member sends in a marketable order, but an order resting on the Exchange order book was subsequently executed, the Missed Liquidity Report can assist the Member in determining by how much time that order missed an execution.
[
12
]
The Missed Liquidity Report includes the following data elements for orders and quotes:
[
13
]
(1) Message Type;
[
14
]
(2) Date; (3) Recipient Member ID; (4) Session Sub ID;
[
15
]
(5) Clearing Identifier;
[
16
]
(6) Client Identifier;
[
17
]
(7) Trade Condition;
[
18
]
(8) Auction ID;
[
19
]
(8) Symbol; (9) Cboe Order ID;
[
20
]
(10) Execution ID;
[
21
]
(11) Exchange System Timestamps for orders, quotes, and cancels;
[
22
]
(12) Matching Unit Number;
[
23
]
(13) Queued;
[
24
]
(14) Port Type;
[
25
]
and (15) Aggressor Order Type.
[
26
]
No specific information about resting orders on the Exchange book will be provided.
Enhancements
As noted above, the Exchange now seeks to update the Cboe Timestamping Service by adding additional data elements to the Missed Liquidity Report. Specifically, the Exchange seeks to enhance the Missed Liquidity Report to include COA and C-AIM events, as well as a new price field that includes each price level at which options orders were executed during an Auction, in
(
printed page 69603)
addition to the Recipient Member's orders, modify message and quotes related to an Auction. Importantly, no other changes will be made to the Missed Liquidity Report, and aside from these proposed enhancements, the Missed Liquidity Report will remain as described above.
As proposed, a Member's options orders, quotes and modify messages that are eligible to participate in an Auction will now appear in the Missed Liquidity Report. The Missed Liquidity Report will now show the Member the time details for their eligible options orders, quotes and modify messages for an Auction, as well as the time details for executions of other COA-eligible and C-AIM-eligible options orders resting on the Complex Order Book (“COB”),
[
27
]
that the Member receiving the Missed Liquidity Report attempted to execute against within an Exchange-determined amount of time (not to exceed 1 millisecond) after receipt of the first attempt to execute against the resting options order and within an Exchange-determined amount of time (not to exceed 100 microseconds) before receipt of the first attempt to execute against the resting options order.
[
28
]
For example, if a Member sends in a COA-eligible options order or a C-AIM-eligible options order (collectively, “Auction Orders”), but a resting options order participating in the Auction was subsequently executed, the Missed Liquidity Report can assist the Member in determining by how much time their options order missed an execution.
Additionally, for Auctions clearing across multiple price levels, the Missed Liquidity Report will now also include a new price field that shows each price level at which (i) the Auction Orders were executed during an Auction; and (ii) the Recipient Member's order, modify messages and quotes were at. This will enable a Member to see where their orders, modify messages, and quotes sat relative to the price levels at which other options orders executed in the Auction.
Generally speaking, the Exchange believes that market participants utilize liquidity accessing orders when there is a high probability that they will execute against an order or quote resting on the Exchange order book. In this regard, the Missed Liquidity Report helps subscribing market participants to better understand by how much time they missed executing against certain resting orders or quotes. The Exchange therefore believes this report will provide greater visibility into what was missed in trading so market participants can better determine whether they want to invest in the technology to mitigate the misses. It may also allow them to optimize their models and trading patterns to yield better execution results. Notably, the proposed additional data elements will further enhance the utility of the Missed Liquidity Report, and provide subscribers with similar insight into the Auctions, as well as better enable them to utilize the data to optimize their models and trading patterns to yield better execution results.
The Exchange notes that even with the enhancements to the Missed Liquidity Report, the data contained within the proposed Missed Liquidity Report is substantially the same data provided by the Exchange today.
Implementation
The Exchange will announce via Exchange Notice the implementation date of the proposed rule change, which shall occur no later than 60 days after the operative date of this rule filing.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
29
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
30
]
in particular, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and to protect investors and the public interest, and that it is not designed to permit unfair discrimination among customers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange also believes this proposal is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because it protects investors and the public interest and promotes just and equitable principles of trade by providing investors with an enhanced option for receiving market data as requested by market participants and Section 6(b)(8) of the Act, which requires that the rules of an exchange not impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
[
31
]
This proposal is in keeping with those principles in that it promotes increased transparency by enhancing the optional Missed Liquidity Report, which will continue to be available to any Member interested in paying to receive it, to include Auction Orders and a new price field reflecting each price level at which options orders were executed during an Auction.
The Exchange also believes this proposal is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because it protects investors and the public interest and promotes just and equitable principles of trade by providing investors with enhanced options for receiving market data as requested by potential purchasers. The proposed enhancements would benefit investors by facilitating their prompt access to additional value-added information regarding their participation in Auctions, which is not currently included in the Missed Liquidity Report. The enhanced report will allow Members to access information regarding their Auction Orders that they may utilize to evaluate their own trading behavior and order interactions in the same manner they currently can for options orders and quotes executing against interest resting on the Exchange order book. It also promotes just and equitable principles of trade because it would provide latency and execution price level information in a systematized way and standardized format to any Member that chooses to subscribe to the Missed Liquidity Report. As discussed, the proposed report is not a real-time market data product, but rather provides only historical trading data for the previous trading day, generally on a T+1 basis, and the Auction Orders data will be provided on the same basis. In addition, the data in the report regarding incoming orders or quotes that failed to execute including options orders that failed to execute in an Auction, would be specific to the Recipient Member's messages. As noted above, no specific information about the resting orders on the Exchange book will be provided and any information relating to another Member would be anonymized.
With respect to the first enhancement, the Exchange believes that including Auction Order events in the Missed Liquidity Report is also consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because it simply extends the report's existing functionality to an additional execution mechanism on the Exchange. Currently, a Member that submits Auction Orders to an Auction receives no insight through the Missed Liquidity Report into how much time its options orders missed executing against other Auction Orders resting on the COB. As proposed, the report will show a Member the time
(
printed page 69604)
details for its eligible options orders, quotes and modify messages in an Auction, as well as time details for executions of other Auction Orders resting on the COB that the Member attempted to execute against, using the same Exchange-determined time parameters (not to exceed 1 millisecond after, and 100 microseconds before, receipt of the first attempt to execute) that currently apply to the report. By applying the same methodology to Auctions, the enhancement will provide Members with greater visibility into what was missed in an Auction, enabling them to better determine whether to invest in technology to mitigate those misses and to optimize their models and trading patterns to yield better execution results in COAs and C-AIMs. The Exchange believes that better informed Members are more likely to participate efficiently in Auctions, which may in turn contribute to more robust price competition in the auction, to the benefit of investors whose complex orders are exposed in an Auction. This furthers the protection of investors and the public interest and removes impediments to and perfects the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system.
With respect to the second enhancement, the Exchange believes that adding a new price field showing each price level at which Auction Orders were executed during a COA or C-AIM clearing across multiple price levels, is likewise consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act. Because an Auction may clear at more than one price, timing information alone may not give a Member a complete picture of why its options order did not execute. The new price field will enable a Member to see where its options orders, quotes and modify messages sat relative to the price levels at which other options orders executed in the Auction, which will help the Member understand whether a missed execution was attributable to timing, price, or both, and to refine its pricing and order submission strategies accordingly. The Exchange notes that the price field identifies only (i) the Member's own pricing for its quotes, orders and modify messages and (ii) the price levels at which executions occurred; it does not identify the Member or other market participant on the other side of any execution, and the report will continue to restrict all market participants from receiving another market participant's data. Accordingly, the Exchange believes the new price field increases the utility and transparency of the report for subscribing Members without disclosing sensitive information about other market participants, thereby promoting just and equitable principles of trade and protecting investors and the public interest.
The Exchange further notes that the proposed enhancements are limited in scope. No other changes will be made to the Missed Liquidity Report, and the Exchange is not proposing any enhancements to the Missed Cancels Report or the All Cancels Report. The enhanced Missed Liquidity Report will continue to be an optional product equally available to all Members on the same terms.
The Exchange notes that the Cboe Timestamping Service, including the Missed Liquidity Report that is the subject of the proposed enhancements, is an existing Exchange market data product that was previously filed
[
32
]
with, and reviewed by, the Commission. In that filing, the Commission waived the 30-day operative delay so that the Exchange could launch the Missed Liquidity Report and Missed Cancels Report on January 27, 2025, finding that doing so was consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest and noting that the filing did not introduce any novel regulatory issues.
[
33
]
The proposed rule change does not alter the fundamental structure or purpose of the Missed Liquidity Report as previously filed. Rather, it applies the report's existing methodology to an additional execution mechanism—Auctions—and adds a related price field, while retaining the same core features already reviewed by the Commission: the report remains optional, is available to all Members, contains only historical data provided on a T+1 basis, and includes only data specific to the Recipient Member.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule changes do not introduce a new product. Rather, the proposed amendments seek to enhance the existing Missed Liquidity Report, which was previously filed with the Commission and became effective upon filing. Accordingly, the Exchange believes the proposed rule changes do not raise any new competitive issues. With respect to intermarket competition, the Exchange believes the proposed additions will enhance competition between exchanges by improving the quality and utility of the Exchange's market data offerings, thereby allowing the Exchange to better compete with other exchanges that offer similar trading-related reports, such as MIAX Emerald's Liquidity Taker Event Report.
[
34
]
Market participants have numerous alternative venues for trading complex orders, and other exchanges remain free to develop and offer similar competing data products.
Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change does not impose any burden on intramarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The enhanced Missed Liquidity Report will be available to all Members on the same terms, and any Member that subscribes to the report will automatically receive the Auction data for its own Auction Orders, quotes and modify messages. The Auction data, including the new price field, will be specific to the Recipient Member's own orders, quotes and modify messages, will be provided only on a historical, T+1 basis, and will not identify any other market participant. As such, the enhancements will not provide any Member with an informational advantage over other market participants in real-time trading. Moreover, market participants are not required to purchase the Missed Liquidity Report, and the Exchange is not required to make the Missed Liquidity Report available to investors. Rather, the Exchange is voluntarily making the Missed Liquidity Report available, as requested by Members, and Members may choose to receive (and pay for) this data based on their own business needs. Potential purchasers may request the data at any time if they believe it to be valuable or may decline to purchase such data.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not:
A. significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest;
(
printed page 69605)
B. impose any significant burden on competition; and
C. become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
35
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
36
]
thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission will institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views, and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-CboeEDGX-2026-073 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-CboeEDGX-2026-073. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-CboeEDGX-2026-073 and should be submitted on or before November 25, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
37
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

full_text:

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106787; File No. SR-CboeBZX-2026-088]
October 30, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 21, 2026, Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “BZX”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Exchange filed the proposal as a “non-controversial” proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
3
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
4
]
The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “BZX Options”) proposes to introduce enhancements to the Missed Liquidity Report offered as part of the Cboe Timestamping Service.
The text of the proposed rule change is also available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
), the Exchange's website (
https://www.cboe.com/​us/​equities/​regulation/​rule_​filings/​bzx/​
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes introduce enhancements to the Cboe Timestamping Service, which is a market data service comprised of the Missed Liquidity Report, Missed Cancels Report and All Cancels Report. Specifically, the Exchange seeks to update the Missed Liquidity Report to
(
printed page 69590)
now include Complex Order Auction (“COA”)
[
5
]
events, as well as a new price field that, for records related to COA, includes each price of the subscribing Member's orders, modify messages, and quotes, as well as each price level at which options orders were executed during a COA. The Exchange is not proposing any enhancements to either the Missed Cancels Report or the All Cancels Report.
[
6
]
Background
Currently, the Cboe Timestamping Service provides timestamp information for orders, quotes and cancels for market participants. More specifically, the Cboe Timestamping Service reports provide various timestamps relating to the message lifecycle throughout the Exchange System.
[
7
]
The reports are optional products that are available to all Members and Members may opt to choose any combination of reports or no reports at all. Corresponding fees are assessed based on the number of reports selected.
[
8
]
Notably, the data included in these reports is based only on the data of the market participant that opts to subscribe to the reports (“Recipient Member”) and does not include information related to any Member other than the Recipient Member. The Exchange restricts all other market participants from receiving another market participant's data. Additionally, no report includes real-time market data. Rather, the reports contain only historical data from the prior trading day and are only available after the end of the trading day, generally on a T+1 basis.
Specifically, the Missed Liquidity Report provides time details for executions of orders and quotes that rest on the BZX Book
[
9
]
where the Member receiving the report attempted to execute against that resting order within an Exchange-determined amount of time (not to exceed 1 millisecond) after receipt of the first attempt to execute against the resting order or quote and within an Exchange-determined amount of time (not to exceed 100 microseconds) before receipt of the first attempt to execute against the resting order or quote.
[
10
]
For example, if a Member sends in a marketable order, but an order resting on the Exchange order book was subsequently executed, the Missed Liquidity Report can assist the Member in determining by how much time that order missed an execution.
[
11
]
The Missed Liquidity Report includes the following data elements for orders and quotes:
[
12
]
(1) Message Type;
[
13
]
(2) Date; (3) Recipient Member ID; (4) Session Sub ID;
[
14
]
(5) Clearing Identifier;
[
15
]
(6) Client Identifier;
[
16
]
(7) Trade Condition;
[
17
]
(8) Symbol; (9) Cboe Order ID;
[
18
]
(10) Execution ID;
[
19
]
(11) Exchange System Timestamps for orders, quotes, and cancels;
[
20
]
(12) Matching Unit Number;
[
21
]
(13) Queued;
[
22
]
(14) Port Type;
[
23
]
and (15) Aggressor Order Type.
[
24
]
No specific information about resting orders on the Exchange book will be provided.
Enhancements
As noted above, the Exchange now seeks to update the Cboe Timestamping Service by adding additional data elements to the Missed Liquidity Report. Specifically, the Exchange seeks to enhance the Missed Liquidity Report to include COA events, as well as a new price field that includes each price level at which options orders were executed during a COA in addition to the Recipient Member's orders, modify message and quotes related to the COA. Importantly, no other changes will be made to the Missed Liquidity Report, and aside from these proposed enhancements, the Missed Liquidity Report will remain as described above.
As proposed, a Member's options orders, quotes and modify messages that are eligible to participate in a COA will now appear in the Missed Liquidity
(
printed page 69591)
Report. The Missed Liquidity Report will now show the Member the time details for their eligible options orders, quotes and modify messages for a COA, as well as the time details for executions of other COA-eligible options orders resting on the Complex Order Book (“COB”),
[
25
]
that the Member receiving the Missed Liquidity Report attempted to execute against within an Exchange-determined amount of time (not to exceed 1 millisecond) after receipt of the first attempt to execute against the resting options order and within an Exchange-determined amount of time (not to exceed 100 microseconds) before receipt of the first attempt to execute against the resting options order.
[
26
]
For example, if a Member sends in a COA-eligible options order, but a resting options order participating in the COA was subsequently executed, the Missed Liquidity Report can assist the Member in determining by how much time their options order missed an execution.
Additionally, for COAs clearing across multiple price levels, the Missed Liquidity Report will now also include a new price field that shows each price level at which (i) the COA-eligible options orders were executed during a COA and (ii) the Recipient Member's order, modify messages and quotes were at. This will enable a Member to see where their orders, modify messages, and quotes sat relative to the price levels at which other options orders executed in the COA.
Generally speaking, the Exchange believes that market participants utilize liquidity accessing orders when there is a high probability that they will execute against an order or quote resting on the Exchange order book. In this regard, the Missed Liquidity Report helps subscribing market participants to better understand by how much time they missed executing against certain resting orders or quotes. The Exchange therefore believes this report will provide greater visibility into what was missed in trading so market participants can better determine whether they want to invest in the technology to mitigate the misses. It may also allow them to optimize their models and trading patterns to yield better execution results. Notably, the proposed additional data elements will further enhance the utility of the Missed Liquidity Report, and provide subscribers with similar insight into the COA, as well as better enable them to utilize the data to optimize their models and trading patterns to yield better execution results.
The Exchange notes that even with the enhancements to the Missed Liquidity Report, the data contained within the proposed Missed Liquidity Report is substantially the same data provided by the Exchange today.
Implementation
The Exchange will announce via Exchange Notice the implementation date of the proposed rule change, which shall occur no later than 60 days after the operative date of this rule filing.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
27
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
28
]
in particular, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and to protect investors and the public interest, and that it is not designed to permit unfair discrimination among customers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange also believes this proposal is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because it protects investors and the public interest and promotes just and equitable principles of trade by providing investors with an enhanced option for receiving market data as requested by market participants and Section 6(b)(8) of the Act, which requires that the rules of an exchange not impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
[
29
]
This proposal is in keeping with those principles in that it promotes increased transparency by enhancing the optional Missed Liquidity Report, which will continue to be available to any Member interested in paying to receive it, to include COA events and a new price field reflecting each price level at which options orders were executed during a COA.
The Exchange also believes this proposal is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because it protects investors and the public interest and promotes just and equitable principles of trade by providing investors with enhanced options for receiving market data as requested by potential purchasers. The proposed enhancements would benefit investors by facilitating their prompt access to additional value-added information regarding their participation in COAs, which is not currently included in the Missed Liquidity Report. The enhanced report will allow Members to access information regarding their COA trading activity that they may utilize to evaluate their own trading behavior and order interactions in the same manner they currently can for options orders and quotes executing against interest resting on the Exchange order book. It also promotes just and equitable principles of trade because it would provide latency and execution price level information in a systematized way and standardized format to any Member that chooses to subscribe to the Missed Liquidity Report. As discussed, the proposed reports is not a real-time market data product, but rather provides only historical trading data for the previous trading day, generally on a T+1 basis, and the COA data will be provided on the same basis. In addition, the data in the report regarding incoming orders or quotes that failed to execute including options orders that failed to execute in a COA, would be specific to the Recipient Member's messages. As noted above, no specific information about the resting orders on the Exchange book will be provided and any information relating to another Member would be anonymized.
With respect to the first enhancement, the Exchange believes that including COA events in the Missed Liquidity Report is also consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because it simply extends the report's existing functionality to an additional execution mechanism on the Exchange. Currently, a Member that submits COA-eligible options orders receives no insight through the Missed Liquidity Report into how much time its options orders missed executing against other COA-eligible options orders resting on the COB. As proposed, the report will show a Member the time details for its eligible options orders, quotes and modify messages in a COA, as well as time details for executions of other COA-eligible options orders resting on the COB that the Member attempted to execute against, using the same Exchange-determined time parameters (not to exceed 1 millisecond after, and 100 microseconds before, receipt of the first attempt to execute) that currently apply to the report. By applying the same methodology to COA activity, the enhancement will provide Members with greater visibility into what was
(
printed page 69592)
missed in COA trading, enabling them to better determine whether to invest in technology to mitigate those misses and to optimize their models and trading patterns to yield better execution results in COAs. The Exchange believes that better informed Members are more likely to participate efficiently in COAs, which may in turn contribute to more robust price competition in the auction, to the benefit of investors whose complex orders are exposed in a COA. This furthers the protection of investors and the public interest and removes impediments to and perfects the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system.
With respect to the second enhancement, the Exchange believes that adding a new price field showing each price level at which COA-eligible options orders were executed during a COA clearing across multiple price levels, is likewise consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act. Because a COA may clear at more than one price, timing information alone may not give a Member a complete picture of why its options order did not execute. The new price field will enable a Member to see where its options orders, quotes and modify messages sat relative to the price levels at which other options orders executed in the COA, which will help the Member understand whether a missed execution was attributable to timing, price, or both, and to refine its pricing and order submission strategies accordingly. The Exchange notes that the price field identifies only (i) the Member's own pricing for its quotes, orders and modify messages and (ii) the price levels at which executions occurred; it does not identify the Member or other market participant on the other side of any execution, and the report will continue to restrict all market participants from receiving another market participant's data. Accordingly, the Exchange believes the new price field increases the utility and transparency of the report for subscribing Members without disclosing sensitive information about other market participants, thereby promoting just and equitable principles of trade and protecting investors and the public interest.
The Exchange further notes that the proposed enhancements are limited in scope. No other changes will be made to the Missed Liquidity Report, and the Exchange is not proposing any enhancements to the Missed Cancels Report or the All Cancels Report. The enhanced Missed Liquidity Report will continue to be an optional product equally available to all Members on the same terms.
The Exchange notes that the Cboe Timestamping Service, including the Missed Liquidity Report that is the subject of the proposed enhancements, is an existing Exchange market data product that was previously filed
[
30
]
with, and reviewed by, the Commission. In that filing, the Commission waived the 30-day operative delay so that the Exchange could launch the Missed Liquidity Report and Missed Cancels Report on January 27, 2025, finding that doing so was consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest and noting that the filing did not introduce any novel regulatory issues.
[
31
]
The proposed rule change does not alter the fundamental structure or purpose of the Missed Liquidity Report as previously filed. Rather, it applies the report's existing methodology to an additional execution mechanism (
i.e.,
COAs) and adds a related price field, while retaining the same core features already reviewed by the Commission: the report remains optional, is available to all Members, contains only historical data provided on a T+1 basis, and includes only data specific to the Recipient Member.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule changes do not introduce a new product. Rather, the proposed amendments seek to enhance the existing Missed Liquidity Report, which was previously filed with the Commission and became effected upon filing. Accordingly, the Exchange believes the proposed rule changes do not raise any new competitive issues. With respect to intermarket competition, the Exchange believes the proposed additions will enhance competition between exchanges by improving the quality and utility of the Exchange's market data offerings, thereby allowing the Exchange to better compete with other exchanges that offer similar trading-related reports, such as MIAX Emerald's Liquidity Taker Event Report.
[
32
]
Market participants have numerous alternative venues for trading complex orders, and other exchanges remain free to develop and offer similar competing data products.
Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change does not impose any burden on intramarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The enhanced Missed Liquidity Report will be available to all Members on the same terms, and any Member that subscribes to the report will automatically receive the COA data for its own COA-eligible options orders, quotes and modify messages. The COA data, including the new price field, will be specific to the Recipient Member's own orders, quotes and modify messages, will be provided only on a historical, T+1 basis, and will not identify any other market participant. As such, the enhancements will not provide any Member with an informational advantage over other market participants in real-time trading. Moreover, market participants are not required to purchase the Missed Liquidity Report, and the Exchange is not required to make the Missed Liquidity Report available to investors. Rather, the Exchange is voluntarily making the Missed Liquidity Report available, as requested by Members, and Members may choose to receive (and pay for) this data based on their own business needs. Potential purchasers may request the data at any time if they believe it to be valuable or may decline to purchase such data.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not:
A. significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest;
B. impose any significant burden on competition; and

full_text:
