Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106786; File No. SR-C2-2026-028]
October 30, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 21, 2026, Cboe C2 Exchange, Inc. (“Exchange” or “C2”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Exchange filed the proposal as a “non-controversial” proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
3
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
4
]
The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe C2 Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “C2”) proposes to introduce enhancements to the Missed Liquidity Report offered as part of the Cboe Timestamping Service.
The text of the proposed rule change is also available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
), the Exchange's website (
https://www.cboe.com/​us/​options/​regulation/​rule_​filings/​ctwo/​
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes introduce enhancements to the Cboe Timestamping Service, which is a market data service comprised of the Missed Liquidity Report, Missed Cancels Report and All Cancels Report. Specifically, the Exchange seeks to update the Missed Liquidity Report to now include Complex Order Auction (“COA”)
[
5
]
events, as well as a new price field that, for records related to COA, includes each price of the subscribing
(
printed page 69607)
Member's orders, modify messages, and quotes, as well as each price level at which options orders were executed during a COA. The Exchange is not proposing any enhancements to either the Missed Cancels Report or the All Cancels Report.
[
6
]
Background
Currently, the Cboe Timestamping Service provides timestamp information for orders, quotes and cancels for market participants. More specifically, the Cboe Timestamping Service reports provide various timestamps relating to the message lifecycle throughout the Exchange System.
[
7
]
The reports are optional products that are available to all Members and Members may opt to choose any combination of reports or no reports at all. Corresponding fees are assessed based on the number of reports selected.
[
8
]
Notably, the data included in these reports is based only on the data of the market participant that opts to subscribe to the reports (“Recipient Member”) and does not include information related to any Member other than the Recipient Member. The Exchange restricts all other market participants from receiving another market participant's data. Additionally, no report includes real-time market data. Rather, the reports contain only historical data from the prior trading day and are only available after the end of the trading day, generally on a T+1 basis.
Specifically, the Missed Liquidity Report provides time details for executions of orders and quotes that rest on the C2 Book
[
9
]
where the Member receiving the report attempted to execute against that resting order within an Exchange-determined amount of time (not to exceed 1 millisecond) after receipt of the first attempt to execute against the resting order or quote and within an Exchange-determined amount of time (not to exceed 100 microseconds) before receipt of the first attempt to execute against the resting order or quote.
[
10
]
For example, if a Member sends in a marketable order, but an order resting on the Exchange order book was subsequently executed, the Missed Liquidity Report can assist the Member in determining by how much time that order missed an execution.
[
11
]
The Missed Liquidity Report includes the following data elements for orders and quotes
[
12
]
and cancel messages,
[
13
]
respectively: (1) Message Type;
[
14
]
(2) Date; (3) Recipient Member ID; (4) Session Sub ID;
[
15
]
(5) Clearing Identifier;
[
16
]
(6) Client Identifier;
[
17
]
(7) Trade Condition;
[
18
]
(8) Auction ID,
[
19
]
(9) Symbol; (10) Cboe Order ID;
[
20
]
(11) Execution ID;
[
21
]
(12) Exchange System Timestamps for orders, quotes, and cancels;
[
22
]
(13) Matching Unit Number;
[
23
]
(14) Queued;
[
24
]
(15) Port Type;
[
25
]
and (16) Aggressor Order Type.
[
26
]
No specific information about resting orders on the Exchange book will be provided.
Enhancements
As noted above, the Exchange now seeks to update the Cboe Timestamping Service by adding additional data elements to the Missed Liquidity Report. Specifically, the Exchange seeks to enhance the Missed Liquidity Report to include COA events, as well as a new price field that includes each price level at which options orders were executed during a COA in addition to the Recipient Member's orders, modify message and quotes related to the COA. Importantly, no other changes will be made to the Missed Liquidity Report, and aside from these proposed enhancements, the Missed Liquidity Report will remain as described above.
(
printed page 69608)
As proposed, a Member's options orders, quotes and modify messages that are eligible to participate in a COA will now appear in the Missed Liquidity Report. The Missed Liquidity Report will now show the Member the time details for their eligible options orders, quotes and modify messages for a COA, as well as the time details for executions of other COA-eligible options orders resting on the Complex Order Book (“COB”),
[
27
]
that the Member receiving the Missed Liquidity Report attempted to execute against within an Exchange-determined amount of time (not to exceed 1 millisecond) after receipt of the first attempt to execute against the resting options order and within an Exchange-determined amount of time (not to exceed 100 microseconds) before receipt of the first attempt to execute against the resting options order.
[
28
]
For example, if a Member sends in a COA-eligible options order, but a resting options order participating in the COA was subsequently executed, the Missed Liquidity Report can assist the Member in determining by how much time their options order missed an execution.
Additionally, for COAs clearing across multiple price levels, the Missed Liquidity Report will now also include a new price field that shows each price level at which (i) the COA-eligible options orders were executed during a COA and (ii) the Recipient Member's order, modify messages and quotes were at. This will enable a Member to see where their orders, modify messages, and quotes sat relative to the price levels at which other options orders executed in the COA.
Generally speaking, the Exchange believes that market participants utilize liquidity accessing orders when there is a high probability that they will execute against an order or quote resting on the Exchange order book. In this regard, the Missed Liquidity Report helps subscribing market participants to better understand by how much time they missed executing against certain resting orders or quotes. The Exchange therefore believes this report will provide greater visibility into what was missed in trading so market participants can better determine whether they want to invest in the technology to mitigate the misses. It may also allow them to optimize their models and trading patterns to yield better execution results. Notably, the proposed additional data elements will further enhance the utility of the Missed Liquidity Report, and provide subscribers with similar insight into the COA, as well as better enable them to utilize the data to optimize their models and trading patterns to yield better execution results.
The Exchange notes that even with the enhancements to the Missed Liquidity Report, the data contained within the proposed Missed Liquidity Report is substantially the same data provided by the Exchange today.
Implementation
The Exchange will announce via Exchange Notice the implementation date of the proposed rule change, which shall occur no later than 60 days after the operative date of this rule filing.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
29
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
30
]
in particular, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and to protect investors and the public interest, and that it is not designed to permit unfair discrimination among customers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange also believes this proposal is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because it protects investors and the public interest and promotes just and equitable principles of trade by providing investors with an enhanced option for receiving market data as requested by market participants and Section 6(b)(8) of the Act, which requires that the rules of an exchange not impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
[
31
]
This proposal is in keeping with those principles in that it promotes increased transparency by enhancing the optional Missed Liquidity Report, which will continue to be available to any Member interested in paying to receive it, to include COA events and a new price field reflecting each price level at which options orders were executed during a COA.
The Exchange also believes this proposal is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because it protects investors and the public interest and promotes just and equitable principles of trade by providing investors with enhanced options for receiving market data as requested by potential purchasers. The proposed enhancements would benefit investors by facilitating their prompt access to additional value-added information regarding their participation in COAs, which is not currently included in the Missed Liquidity Report. The enhanced report will allow Members to access information regarding their COA trading activity that they may utilize to evaluate their own trading behavior and order interactions in the same manner they currently can for options orders and quotes executing against interest resting on the Exchange order book. It also promotes just and equitable principles of trade because it would provide latency and execution price level information in a systematized way and standardized format to any Member that chooses to subscribe to the Missed Liquidity Report. As discussed, the proposed reports is not a real-time market data product, but rather provides only historical trading data for the previous trading day, generally on a T+1 basis, and the COA data will be provided on the same basis. In addition, the data in the report regarding incoming orders or quotes that failed to execute including options orders that failed to execute in a COA, would be specific to the Recipient Member's messages. As noted above, no specific information about the resting orders on the Exchange book will be provided and any information relating to another Member would be anonymized.
With respect to the first enhancement, the Exchange believes that including COA events in the Missed Liquidity Report is also consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because it simply extends the report's existing functionality to an additional execution mechanism on the Exchange. Currently, a Member that submits COA-eligible options orders receives no insight through the Missed Liquidity Report into how much time its options orders missed executing against other COA-eligible options orders resting on the COB. As proposed, the report will show a Member the time details for its eligible options orders, quotes and modify messages in a COA, as well as time details for executions of other COA-eligible options orders resting on the COB that the Member attempted to execute against, using the same Exchange-determined time parameters (not to exceed 1 millisecond after, and 100 microseconds before, receipt of the
(
printed page 69609)
first attempt to execute) that currently apply to the report. By applying the same methodology to COA activity, the enhancement will provide Members with greater visibility into what was missed in COA trading, enabling them to better determine whether to invest in technology to mitigate those misses and to optimize their models and trading patterns to yield better execution results in COAs. The Exchange believes that better informed Members are more likely to participate efficiently in COAs, which may in turn contribute to more robust price competition in the auction, to the benefit of investors whose complex orders are exposed in a COA. This furthers the protection of investors and the public interest and removes impediments to and perfects the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system.
With respect to the second enhancement, the Exchange believes that adding a new price field showing each price level at which COA-eligible options orders were executed during a COA clearing across multiple price levels, is likewise consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act. Because a COA may clear at more than one price, timing information alone may not give a Member a complete picture of why its options order did not execute. The new price field will enable a Member to see where its options orders, quotes and modify messages sat relative to the price levels at which other options orders executed in the COA, which will help the Member understand whether a missed execution was attributable to timing, price, or both, and to refine its pricing and order submission strategies accordingly. The Exchange notes that the price field identifies only (i) the Member's own pricing for its quotes, orders and modify messages and (ii) the price levels at which executions occurred; it does not identify the Member or other market participant on the other side of any execution, and the report will continue to restrict all market participants from receiving another market participant's data. Accordingly, the Exchange believes the new price field increases the utility and transparency of the report for subscribing Members without disclosing sensitive information about other market participants, thereby promoting just and equitable principles of trade and protecting investors and the public interest.
The Exchange further notes that the proposed enhancements are limited in scope. No other changes will be made to the Missed Liquidity Report, and the Exchange is not proposing any enhancements to the Missed Cancels Report or the All Cancels Report. The enhanced Missed Liquidity Report will continue to be an optional product equally available to all Members on the same terms.
The Exchange notes that the Cboe Timestamping Service, including the Missed Liquidity Report that is the subject of the proposed enhancements, is an existing Exchange market data product that was previously filed
[
32
]
with, and reviewed by, the Commission. In that filing, the Commission waived the 30-day operative delay so that the Exchange could launch the Missed Liquidity Report and Missed Cancels Report on January 27, 2025, finding that doing so was consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest and noting that the filing did not introduce any novel regulatory issues.
[
33
]
The proposed rule change does not alter the fundamental structure or purpose of the Missed Liquidity Report as previously filed. Rather, it applies the report's existing methodology to an additional execution mechanism (
i.e.,
COAs) and adds a related price field, while retaining the same core features already reviewed by the Commission: the report remains optional, is available to all Members, contains only historical data provided on a T+1 basis, and includes only data specific to the Recipient Member.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule changes do not introduce a new product. Rather, the proposed amendments seek to enhance the existing Missed Liquidity Report, which was previously filed with the Commission and became effected upon filing. Accordingly, the Exchange believes the proposed rule changes do not raise any new competitive issues. With respect to intermarket competition, the Exchange believes the proposed additions will enhance competition between exchanges by improving the quality and utility of the Exchange's market data offerings, thereby allowing the Exchange to better compete with other exchanges that offer similar trading-related reports, such as MIAX Emerald's Liquidity Taker Event Report.
[
34
]
Market participants have numerous alternative venues for trading complex orders, and other exchanges remain free to develop and offer similar competing data products.
Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change does not impose any burden on intramarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The enhanced Missed Liquidity Report will be available to all Members on the same terms, and any Member that subscribes to the report will automatically receive the COA data for its own COA-eligible options orders, quotes and modify messages. The COA data, including the new price field, will be specific to the Recipient Member's own orders, quotes and modify messages, will be provided only on a historical, T+1 basis, and will not identify any other market participant. As such, the enhancements will not provide any Member with an informational advantage over other market participants in real-time trading. Moreover, market participants are not required to purchase the Missed Liquidity Report, and the Exchange is not required to make the Missed Liquidity Report available to investors. Rather, the Exchange is voluntarily making the Missed Liquidity Report available, as requested by Members, and Members may choose to receive (and pay for) this data based on their own business needs. Potential purchasers may request the data at any time if they believe it to be valuable or may decline to purchase such data.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not:
A. significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest;
B. impose any significant burden on competition; and
C. become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
35
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
36
]
thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change,
(
printed page 69610)
the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission will institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views, and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-C2-2026-028 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-C2-2026-028. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-C2-2026-028 and should be submitted on or before November 25, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
37
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106785; File No. SR-CBOE-2026-083]
October 30, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 21, 2026, Cboe Exchange, Inc. (“Exchange” or “Cboe Options”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Exchange filed the proposal as a “non-controversial” proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
3
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
4
]
The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “Cboe Options”) proposes to introduce enhancements to the Missed Liquidity Report offered as part of the Cboe Timestamping Service.
The text of the proposed rule change is also available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
), the Exchange's website (
https://www.cboe.com/​us/​options/​regulation/​rule_​filings/​cone/​
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes introduce enhancements to the Cboe Timestamping Service, which is a market data service comprised of the Missed Liquidity Report, Missed Cancels Report and All Cancels Report. Specifically, the Exchange seeks to update the Missed Liquidity Report to now include Complex Order Auction (“COA”)
[
5
]
and Complex Automated Improvement Mechanism (“C-AIM”)
[
6
]
events (collectively, “Auction Orders” or an “Auction”), as well as a new price field that, for records related to Auction Orders, includes each price of the subscribing Member's orders, modify messages, and quotes, as well as each price level at which options orders were executed during an Auction. The Exchange is not proposing any enhancements to either the Missed Cancels Report or the All Cancels Report.
[
7
]
Currently, the Cboe Timestamping Service provides timestamp information for orders, quotes and cancels for market participants. More specifically, the Cboe Timestamping Service reports provide various timestamps relating to the message lifecycle throughout the Exchange System.
[
8
]
The reports are optional products that are available to all Members and Members may opt to choose any combination of reports or no reports at all. Corresponding fees are assessed based on the number of reports selected.
[
9
]
Notably, the data included in these reports is based only on the data of the market participant that opts to subscribe to the reports (“Recipient Member”) and does not include information related to any Member other than the Recipient Member. The Exchange restricts all other market participants from receiving
(
printed page 69617)
another market participant's data. Additionally, no report includes real-time market data. Rather, the reports contain only historical data from the prior trading day and are only available after the end of the trading day, generally on a T+1 basis.
Specifically, the Missed Liquidity Report provides time details for executions of orders and quotes that rest on the book where the Member receiving the report attempted to execute against that resting order within an Exchange-determined amount of time (not to exceed 1 millisecond) after receipt of the first attempt to execute against the resting order or quote and within an Exchange-determined amount of time (not to exceed 100 microseconds) before receipt of the first attempt to execute against the resting order or quote.
[
10
]
For example, if a Member sends in a marketable order, but an order resting on the Exchange order book was subsequently executed, the Missed Liquidity Report can assist the Member in determining by how much time that order missed an execution.
[
11
]
The Missed Liquidity Report includes the following data elements for orders and quotes:
[
12
]
(1) Message Type;
[
13
]
(2) Date; (3) Recipient Member ID; (4) Session Sub ID;
[
14
]
(5) Clearing Identifier;
[
15
]
(6) Client Identifier;
[
16
]
(7) Trade Condition;
[
17
]
(8) Auction ID,
[
18
]
(9) Symbol; (10) Cboe Order ID;
[
19
]
(11) Execution ID;
[
20
]
(12) Exchange System Timestamps for orders, quotes, and cancels;
[
21
]
(13) Matching Unit Number;
[
22
]
(14) Queued;
[
23
]
(15) Port Type;
[
24
]
and (16) Aggressor Order Type.
[
25
]
No specific information about resting orders on the Exchange book will be provided.
Enhancements
As noted above, the Exchange now seeks to update the Cboe Timestamping Service by adding additional data elements to the Missed Liquidity Report. Specifically, the Exchange seeks to enhance the Missed Liquidity Report to include COA and C-AIM events, as well as a new price field that includes each price level at which options orders were executed during an Auction, in addition to the Recipient Member's orders, modify message and quotes related to an Auction. Importantly, no other changes will be made to the Missed Liquidity Report, and aside from these proposed enhancements, the Missed Liquidity Report will remain as described above.
As proposed, a Member's options orders, quotes and modify messages that are eligible to participate in an Auction will now appear in the Missed Liquidity Report. The Missed Liquidity Report will now show the Member the time details for their eligible options orders, quotes and modify messages for an Auction, as well as the time details for executions of other COA-eligible and C-AIM-eligible options orders resting on the Complex Order Book (“COB”),
[
26
]
that the Member receiving the Missed Liquidity Report attempted to execute against within an Exchange-determined amount of time (not to exceed 1 millisecond) after receipt of the first attempt to execute against the resting options order and within an Exchange-determined amount of time (not to exceed 100 microseconds) before receipt of the first attempt to execute against the resting options order.
[
27
]
For example, if a Member sends in a COA-eligible options order or a C-AIM-eligible options order (collectively, “Auction Orders”), but a resting options order participating in the Auction was subsequently executed, the Missed Liquidity Report can assist the Member in determining by how much time their options order missed an execution.
Additionally, for Auctions clearing across multiple price levels, the Missed Liquidity Report will now also include a new price field that shows each price level at which (i) the Auction Orders were executed during an Auction; and (ii) the Recipient Member's order, modify messages and quotes were at. This will enable a Member to see where their orders, modify messages, and quotes sat relative to the price levels at
(
printed page 69618)
which other options orders executed in the Auction.
Generally speaking, the Exchange believes that market participants utilize liquidity accessing orders when there is a high probability that they will execute against an order or quote resting on the Exchange order book. In this regard, the Missed Liquidity Report helps subscribing market participants to better understand by how much time they missed executing against certain resting orders or quotes. The Exchange therefore believes this report will provide greater visibility into what was missed in trading so market participants can better determine whether they want to invest in the technology to mitigate the misses. It may also allow them to optimize their models and trading patterns to yield better execution results. Notably, the proposed additional data elements will further enhance the utility of the Missed Liquidity Report, and provide subscribers with similar insight into the Auctions, as well as better enable them to utilize the data to optimize their models and trading patterns to yield better execution results.
The Exchange notes that even with the enhancements to the Missed Liquidity Report, the data contained within the proposed Missed Liquidity Report is substantially the same data provided by the Exchange today.
Implementation
The Exchange will announce via Exchange Notice the implementation date of the proposed rule change, which shall occur no later than 60 days after the operative date of this rule filing.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
28
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
29
]
in particular, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and to protect investors and the public interest, and that it is not designed to permit unfair discrimination among customers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange also believes this proposal is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because it protects investors and the public interest and promotes just and equitable principles of trade by providing investors with an enhanced option for receiving market data as requested by market participants and Section 6(b)(8) of the Act, which requires that the rules of an exchange not impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
[
30
]
This proposal is in keeping with those principles in that it promotes increased transparency by enhancing the optional Missed Liquidity Report, which will continue to be available to any Member interested in paying to receive it, to include Auction Orders and a new price field reflecting each price level at which options orders were executed during an Auction.
The Exchange also believes this proposal is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because it protects investors and the public interest and promotes just and equitable principles of trade by providing investors with enhanced options for receiving market data as requested by potential purchasers. The proposed enhancements would benefit investors by facilitating their prompt access to additional value-added information regarding their participation in Auctions, which is not currently included in the Missed Liquidity Report. The enhanced report will allow Members to access information regarding their Auction Orders that they may utilize to evaluate their own trading behavior and order interactions in the same manner they currently can for options orders and quotes executing against interest resting on the Exchange order book. It also promotes just and equitable principles of trade because it would provide latency and execution price level information in a systematized way and standardized format to any Member that chooses to subscribe to the Missed Liquidity Report. As discussed, the proposed report is not a real-time market data product, but rather provides only historical trading data for the previous trading day, generally on a T+1 basis, and the Auction Orders data will be provided on the same basis. In addition, the data in the report regarding incoming orders or quotes that failed to execute including options orders that failed to execute in an Auction, would be specific to the Recipient Member's messages. As noted above, no specific information about the resting orders on the Exchange book will be provided and any information relating to another Member would be anonymized.
With respect to the first enhancement, the Exchange believes that including Auction Order events in the Missed Liquidity Report is also consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because it simply extends the report's existing functionality to an additional execution mechanism on the Exchange. Currently, a Member that submits Auction Orders to an Auction receives no insight through the Missed Liquidity Report into how much time its options orders missed executing against other Auction Orders resting on the COB. As proposed, the report will show a Member the time details for its eligible options orders, quotes and modify messages in an Auction, as well as time details for executions of other Auction Orders resting on the COB that the Member attempted to execute against, using the same Exchange-determined time parameters (not to exceed 1 millisecond after, and 100 microseconds before, receipt of the first attempt to execute) that currently apply to the report. By applying the same methodology to Auctions, the enhancement will provide Members with greater visibility into what was missed in an Auction, enabling them to better determine whether to invest in technology to mitigate those misses and to optimize their models and trading patterns to yield better execution results in COAs and C-AIMs. The Exchange believes that better informed Members are more likely to participate efficiently in Auctions, which may in turn contribute to more robust price competition in the auction, to the benefit of investors whose complex orders are exposed in an Auction. This furthers the protection of investors and the public interest and removes impediments to and perfects the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system.
With respect to the second enhancement, the Exchange believes that adding a new price field showing each price level at which Auction Orders were executed during a COA or C-AIM clearing across multiple price levels, is likewise consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act. Because an Auction may clear at more than one price, timing information alone may not give a Member a complete picture of why its options order did not execute. The new price field will enable a Member to see where its options orders, quotes and modify messages sat relative to the price levels at which other options orders executed in the Auction, which will help the Member understand whether a missed execution was attributable to timing, price, or both, and to refine its pricing and order submission strategies accordingly. The Exchange notes that the price field identifies only (i) the Member's own
(
printed page 69619)
pricing for its quotes, orders and modify messages and (ii) the price levels at which executions occurred; it does not identify the Member or other market participant on the other side of any execution, and the report will continue to restrict all market participants from receiving another market participant's data. Accordingly, the Exchange believes the new price field increases the utility and transparency of the report for subscribing Members without disclosing sensitive information about other market participants, thereby promoting just and equitable principles of trade and protecting investors and the public interest.
The Exchange further notes that the proposed enhancements are limited in scope. No other changes will be made to the Missed Liquidity Report, and the Exchange is not proposing any enhancements to the Missed Cancels Report or the All Cancels Report. The enhanced Missed Liquidity Report will continue to be an optional product equally available to all Members on the same terms.
The Exchange notes that the Cboe Timestamping Service, including the Missed Liquidity Report that is the subject of the proposed enhancements, is an existing Exchange market data product that was previously filed
[
31
]
with, and reviewed by, the Commission. In that filing, the Commission waived the 30-day operative delay so that the Exchange could launch the Missed Liquidity Report and Missed Cancels Report on January 27, 2025, finding that doing so was consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest and noting that the filing did not introduce any novel regulatory issues.
[
32
]
The proposed rule change does not alter the fundamental structure or purpose of the Missed Liquidity Report as previously filed. Rather, it applies the report's existing methodology to an additional execution mechanism—Auctions—and adds a related price field, while retaining the same core features already reviewed by the Commission: the report remains optional, is available to all Members, contains only historical data provided on a T+1 basis, and includes only data specific to the Recipient Member.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule changes do not introduce a new product. Rather, the proposed amendments seek to enhance the existing Missed Liquidity Report, which was previously filed with the Commission and became effective upon filing. Accordingly, the Exchange believes the proposed rule changes do not raise any new competitive issues. With respect to intermarket competition, the Exchange believes the proposed additions will enhance competition between exchanges by improving the quality and utility of the Exchange's market data offerings, thereby allowing the Exchange to better compete with other exchanges that offer similar trading-related reports, such as MIAX Emerald's Liquidity Taker Event Report.
[
33
]
Market participants have numerous alternative venues for trading complex orders, and other exchanges remain free to develop and offer similar competing data products.
Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change does not impose any burden on intramarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The enhanced Missed Liquidity Report will be available to all Members on the same terms, and any Member that subscribes to the report will automatically receive the Auction data for its own Auction Orders, quotes and modify messages. The Auction data, including the new price field, will be specific to the Recipient Member's own orders, quotes and modify messages, will be provided only on a historical, T+1 basis, and will not identify any other market participant. As such, the enhancements will not provide any Member with an informational advantage over other market participants in real-time trading. Moreover, market participants are not required to purchase the Missed Liquidity Report, and the Exchange is not required to make the Missed Liquidity Report available to investors. Rather, the Exchange is voluntarily making the Missed Liquidity Report available, as requested by Members, and Members may choose to receive (and pay for) this data based on their own business needs. Potential purchasers may request the data at any time if they believe it to be valuable or may decline to purchase such data.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not:
A. significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest;
B. impose any significant burden on competition; and
C. become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
34
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
35
]
thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission will institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views, and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-CBOE-2026-083  on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-CBOE-2026-083. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use
(
printed page 69620)
only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-CBOE-2026-083 and should be submitted on or before November 25, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
36
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106784; File No. SR-NSCC-2026-012]
October 30, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”)
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 20, 2026, National Securities Clearing Corporation (“NSCC”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II and III below, which Items have been prepared by the clearing agency. NSCC filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
3
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
4
]
The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Clearing Agency's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The proposed rule change consists of modifications to the NSCC Rules & Procedures (“NSCC Rules”) to enhance NSCC's automated reasonability checks for the submission of exchange-traded fund (“ETF”) creation and redemption transactions.
[
5
]
II. Clearing Agency's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the clearing agency included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The clearing agency has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
(A) Clearing Agency's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The purpose of this proposed rule change is to amend the NSCC Rules to enhance NSCC's automated reasonability checks for the submission of ETF creation and redemption transactions by including authorized participants that are Members of NSCC in the reasonability check process and clarifying certain obligations of Index Receipt Agents and authorized participants with respect to this process. Specifically, NSCC proposes to modify the NSCC Rules to (i) include authorized participants in the ETF reasonability check process; (ii) clarify that Index Receipt Agents and authorized participants are required to subscribe to NSCC's designated communication method for pended transaction data and identify and regularly maintain contact persons authorized to receive notifications and review and confirm the validity of pended transactions (such persons being “authorized approvers”); and (iii) clarify requirements concerning the form, manner and timing for such confirmations.
The proposed rule change is discussed in detail below.
Background
ETFs (referred to as “index receipts” in the NSCC Rules) are marketable securities that track stock indices, commodities, bonds, or baskets of assets. ETFs are listed on exchanges and are traded throughout the trading day. Shares of ETFs are created and redeemed in the primary market and are traded on listed exchanges in the secondary market. Each share of an ETF represents an undivided interest in the underlying assets of the ETF.
NSCC facilitates central counterparty clearing and settlement of the creation and redemption of ETF shares in the primary market as well as clearing of ETF trades in the secondary market. The participants in the ETF primary market typically consist of the issuers of ETFs (“ETF Sponsors”), custodian banks (“ETF Agents,” also referred to as “Index Receipt Agents” in the NSCC Rules), and brokers/dealers that have agreements directly with ETF Sponsors to allow the brokers/dealers to place orders for the creation and redemption of ETF shares (referred to as “authorized participants”).
[
6
]
Both ETF Agents and
(
printed page 69611)
authorized participants are Members of NSCC.
In general, authorized participants create and redeem ETF shares from the ETF Sponsors in blocks called “creation units.” An authorized participant that purchases a creation unit of ETF shares delivers a “basket” of securities and other assets to the ETF Agent and then receives the creation unit of ETF shares in return for those assets. The redemption process is the reverse of the creation process; the authorized participant redeems a creation unit of ETF shares in exchange for a basket of securities and other assets. These creation and redemption baskets are referred to as “trading baskets.” NSCC supports the creation and redemption of ETFs on both an “in-kind” and “cash-only” basis.
[
7
]
Under the NSCC Rules, Index Receipt Agents are authorized to submit creation and redemption transaction data on behalf of other Members (
i.e.,
authorized participants).
[
8
]
The obligations of the Member reflected in such transaction data are deemed to have been confirmed and acknowledged by each Member or designated by the Index Receipt Agent as a party thereto and to have been adopted by such Member.
[
9
]
Pursuant to Section F.2. of Procedure II of the NSCC Rules, NSCC performs automated reasonability checks on creation and redemption transaction data submitted by Index Receipt Agents and may pend any transaction data that exceeds certain thresholds established by NSCC.
[
10
]
If NSCC pends any transaction data that exceeds the pre-established thresholds, NSCC notifies the Index Receipt Agent of any transaction data that NSCC has pended. The Index Receipt Agent must then provide confirmation, in the form and within the timeframe required by NSCC, that such pended transaction data should be accepted by NSCC. If the Index Receipt Agent fails to provide such confirmation, the pended transaction data is rejected.
NSCC's current reasonability checks pend any transactions (i) with a total settlement value of $15 billion or greater or (ii) when the variance between the net asset value (“NAV”) on the order and the prior day's closing NAV is 98% or greater in either direction.
[
11
]
Pursuant to the NSCC Rules, NSCC has the authority to adjust thresholds from time to time and may consider feedback from its Members or market conditions when considering adjustments to such thresholds.
[
12
]
NSCC's ETF reasonability checks were designed to provide ETF Agents with an opportunity to review and confirm certain potentially misvalued transactions that have been submitted to NSCC before such transactions are processed by NSCC and before the potentially misvalued transactions would be able to have an impact on, for example, a Member's daily Clearing Fund requirements.
[
13
]
NSCC is now proposing to enhance this process to further minimize the risk of processing misvalued or erroneous transactions.
Proposed Changes
NSCC proposes to enhance its ETF reasonability check process by including the authorized participants that are Members of NSCC in the reasonability check process and clarifying certain obligations of Index Receipt Agents and such authorized participants with respect to this process. Specifically, NSCC proposes to modify the NSCC Rules to (i) include authorized participants in the ETF reasonability check process; (ii) clarify that Index Receipt Agents and authorized participants are required to subscribe to NSCC's designated communication method for pended transaction data and identify and regularly maintain authorized approvers for pended transactions; and (iii) clarify requirements concerning the form, manner and timing of confirmations of pended transactions.
Proposed Inclusion of Authorized Participants in the Reasonability Check Process
NSCC proposes to enhance its ETF reasonability checks by including authorized participants that are Members in the reasonability check process. The proposed rule change would require that, in addition to Index Receipt Agents, authorized participants that are Members of NSCC also review and separately confirm pended transaction data prior to NSCC accepting and guaranteeing such transactions.
To implement the proposed change, NSCC would modify the first paragraph of Section F.2 of Procedure II of the NSCC Rules to provide that NSCC would notify the Index Receipt Agent and authorized participant, rather than solely the Index Receipt Agent, of any transaction data that NSCC has pended. NSCC would also modify Section F.2 of Procedure II to state that the Index Receipt Agent and authorized participant should each review and confirm or reject any pended transaction data.
As discussed above, NSCC's ETF create/redeem reasonability checks were designed to provide ETF Agents with an opportunity to review and confirm certain potentially misvalued transactions that have been submitted to NSCC before such transactions are processed by NSCC and before the potentially misvalued transactions would be able to have an impact on, for example, a Member's daily Clearing Fund requirements.
[
14
]
The acceptance and guarantee of misvalued or erroneous transactions may also result in incorrect and potentially outsized liquidity obligations
[
15
]
or settlement obligations for Members. The proposed rule change would include authorized participants that are NSCC Members in the reasonability check process and clarify that Index Receipt Agents and authorized participants should each affirmatively review and take action upon the notification of any pended transactions. NSCC believes that providing an opportunity for the authorized participant to the transaction to also review and confirm transaction
(
printed page 69612)
data that exceeds NSCC's reasonability check thresholds would reduce the likelihood of NSCC processing misvalued or erroneous transactions and mitigate the risks that may arise from incorrect Clearing Fund, liquidity or settlement obligations due to such misvalued or erroneous transactions.
Proposed Clarifications Regarding Notifications and Contact Persons
NSCC proposes to clarify in the NSCC Rules certain requirements for Index Receipt Agents and authorized participants to (i) subscribe to NSCC's designated communication method for notifying Members of pended creation or redemption transaction data and (ii) identify and regularly maintain contact persons with appropriate knowledge and authority to receive notifications and review and confirm the validity of pended transactions (
i.e.,
“authorized approvers”).
To implement the proposed change, NSCC would add new rule text to Section F.2 of Procedure II of the NSCC Rules to provide that each Index Receipt Agent and authorized participant shall (i) subscribe to NSCC's designated communication method for pended transaction data and (ii) identify and regularly maintain, in such form and in such manner as required by NSCC, contact persons with appropriate knowledge and authority to receive notifications and review and confirm the validity of pended transactions (“authorized approver(s)”).
Section 1.C. of Addendum B of the NSCC Rules requires that an applicant or Member of NSCC shall be qualified for membership if it is able to satisfactorily communicate with NSCC and fulfill anticipated commitments to and meet the operational requirements of NSCC with necessary promptness and accuracy and to conform to any condition and requirement that NSCC reasonably deems necessary for its protection.
[
16
]
Under Section F.2 of Procedure II of the NSCC Rules, NSCC performs reasonability checks and notifies Index Receipt Agents (and as proposed, authorized participants) of any transaction data that NSCC has pended so that such transaction can be confirmed or rejected. The proposed rule change would clarify and codify specific expectations and obligations for Index Receipt Agents and authorized participants with respect to the receipt,
[
17
]
review and confirmation of such pended transaction data. This includes ensuring that Index Receipt Agents and authorized participants are subscribed to necessary notifications and identifying to NSCC the authorized approvers
[
18
]
who are responsible for reviewing and confirming such transactions
[
19
]
to ensure that they can satisfactorily communicate with NSCC and fulfill anticipated commitments to and meet the operational requirements of NSCC with necessary promptness and accuracy in accordance with the NSCC Rules.
Proposed Clarifications Regarding Confirmation Requirements and Timeframes
Finally, the proposed rule change would provide additional clarity regarding the requirements concerning the form, manner and timing of confirmations for pended ETF creation and redemption transactions. As discussed above, Section F.2 of Procedure II of the NSCC Rules currently requires Index Receipt Agents to provide confirmation of pended transactions “in the form and within the timeframe required” by NSCC. The procedure further provides that if the Index Receipt Agent fails to provide such confirmation, such pended transaction data will be rejected. Additionally, the procedure states that NSCC may, in its sole discretion, adjust thresholds from time to time and may consider feedback from its Members or market conditions.
The proposed rule change would clarify that confirmations must be provided by authorized approvers at both the Index Receipt Agent and authorized participant, and that such confirmations must be in the form of a written confirmation and include supporting information explaining the validity of the transaction data in order for the pended transactions to be accepted by NSCC. In addition, the proposed rule change would clarify that NSCC maintains authority to periodically adjust both its reasonability check thresholds and the required timeframes for confirmations.
To implement the proposed change, NSCC would modify Section F.2 of Procedure II of the NSCC Rules to provide that the “authorized approver(s)” at the Index Receipt Agent “and authorized participant” must “each, separately,” provide “written” confirmation, “including supporting information explaining the validity of the transaction data,” in the form and within the timeframe required by NSCC, that such pended transaction data should be accepted by NSCC. NSCC would also modify the procedure to provide that if “either the authorized approver” at the Index Receipt Agent “or authorized participant” fails to provide such confirmation within the required timeframe, such pended transaction data will be rejected. In addition, NSCC would modify Section F.2 of Procedure II of the NSCC Rules to state that NSCC may from time to time “adjust reasonability check thresholds and the required timeframes for confirmations, taking into consideration factors including but not limited to” feedback from its Members or market conditions.
NSCC currently runs several processing cycles for ETF creation and redemption transactions. These include a Same Day Settling (“SDS”) cycle that closes at approximately 1:30 p.m. Eastern Time, a Primary cycle that closes at approximately 8:45 p.m. Eastern Time, and a Supplemental cycle that closes at approximately 11:30 p.m. Eastern Time. SDS creation and redemption transactions are submitted for inclusion in the SDS cycle while T+1 and extended settlement creation and redemption transactions are submitted for inclusion in the Primary or Supplemental cycle. NSCC has established separate required timeframes for the confirmation of pended ETF creations/redemptions submitted for inclusion in the SDS cycle and pended ETF creation/redemption transactions submitted for T+1 or extended settlement for inclusion in the Primary or Supplemental cycles. These required timeframes are designed to provide sufficient time for Index Receipt Agents (and authorized participants, as proposed herein) to review and confirm or reject transactions and for any confirmed transactions to be reviewed, processed and released from pending status by NSCC prior to the cutoff time of the relevant ETF processing cycle.
20
(
printed page 69613)
The release of pended orders after Index Receipt Agent and authorized participant confirmation involves additional processing within NSCC and, in some cases, may require additional, escalated confirmations from the Index Receipt Agent or authorized participant to satisfy the confirmation requirements. As a result, ETF creation and redemption transactions that are (i) not confirmed by an authorized approver(s) and/or (ii) without sufficient supporting information explaining the validity of the transaction data within the required timeframes may not be released for processing and would need to be resubmitted.
The proposed rule change would provide further clarity regarding the required form of confirmation and the applicability of such requirements and timeframes to the ultimate acceptance or rejection of pended ETF creation and redemption transactions. The proposed rule change would make clear to Index Receipt Agents and authorized participants that confirmation of a pended transaction must be provided by an authorized approver in writing, and that such confirmations must include supporting information explaining the validity of the transaction data,
[
21
]
within the required timeframes, in order for a pended transaction to be accepted by NSCC.
NSCC believes the proposed rule change would improve Members' understanding of the reasonability check process and the requirements for confirming transactions so that valid pended ETF transactions can be timely confirmed and accepted by NSCC into their intended ETF processing cycle while mitigating the risk of NSCC processing misvalued or erroneous transactions.
Implementation Timeframe
NSCC would implement the proposed rule change on November 23, 2026.
2. Statutory Basis
NSCC believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to a registered clearing agency. Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act
[
22
]
requires that the rules of a clearing agency be designed to, among other things, promote the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions. NSCC believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act for the reasons stated below.
As described above, NSCC proposes to enhance its automated reasonability checks for the submission of ETF creation and redemption transactions by including authorized participants that are Members of NSCC in the reasonability check process and clarifying certain obligations of Index Receipt Agents and such authorized participants with respect to the reasonability check and confirmation process. The ETF create/redeem reasonability checks currently provide ETF Agents with an opportunity to review and confirm certain potentially misvalued or erroneous transactions that have been submitted to NSCC before such transactions are processed by NSCC. The proposed rule change would provide for an additional layer of review and confirmation by the authorized participants to the transactions and further reduce the likelihood of NSCC processing misvalued or erroneous transactions. In turn, this would further mitigate the risks that may arise from incorrect and potentially outsized Clearing Fund, liquidity or settlement obligations caused by misvalued or erroneous transactions. The proposed rule change would also clarify requirements concerning method of receipt of notifications for pended transactions and the form, manner and timing of confirmations needed to confirm pended transaction data to ensure that Index Receipt Agents and authorized participants can satisfactorily communicate with NSCC and fulfill anticipated commitments to and meet the operational requirements of NSCC with necessary promptness and accuracy, as required by NSCC's membership standards. NSCC believes the proposed rule change would improve Members' understanding of the reasonability check process and the requirements for confirming transactions, thereby improving the efficiency and effectiveness of the reasonability check process. Taken together, the proposed rule change would enhance the process for reviewing and confirming pended transactions so that such transactions can be promptly and accurately included in their intended ETF processing cycle while reducing the likelihood that misvalued or erroneous transactions are allowed to proceed through NSCC's clearing and settlement processes. NSCC therefore believes the proposed rule change would promote the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions in accordance with the requirements of Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act.
[
23
]
(B) Clearing Agency's Statement on Burden on Competition
Section 17A(b)(3)(I) of the Act
[
24
]
requires that the rules of the clearing agency do not impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the Act. NSCC does not believe that the proposed rule change would impose a burden or otherwise have an impact on competition. The proposed rule change would not impact Members' general ability to engage in ETF creation or redemption transactions or to submit such transactions to NSCC for clearing and settlement. The proposed rule change would provide an opportunity for the authorized participant to the transaction to review and confirm transaction data that exceeds NSCC's reasonability check thresholds and reduce the likelihood of NSCC processing a misvalued or erroneous transaction for such Members. The proposed rule change would also provide further clarity regarding the required form, manner and timing of the confirmation of pended transactions. Section F.2 of Procedure II of the NSCC Rules currently requires Index Receipt Agents to provide confirmation of pended transactions “in the form and within the timeframe required” by NSCC. The proposed rule change would clarify that Index Receipt Agents and authorized participants must provide written confirmations by an authorized approver, including supporting information explaining the validity of the transaction data, within required timeframes, and that the failure to provide such confirmation within required timeframes will result in the ultimate rejection of such transactions. Finally, the proposed rule change would clarify and codify specific obligations for Index Receipt Agents and authorized participants to subscribe to necessary notifications and maintain authorized approver contacts for notifications and confirmations to ensure that they can satisfactorily communicate with NSCC and fulfill anticipated commitments to and meet the operational requirements of NSCC with necessary promptness and accuracy, as required by Section 1.C. of Addendum B of the NSCC Rules. NSCC
(
printed page 69614)
believes the proposed rule change would improve Members' understanding of the reasonability check process and the requirements for confirming pended transactions and thereby improve the efficiency and effectiveness of NSCC's ETF reasonability checks. For these reasons, NSCC believes the proposed rule change would not impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the Act.
(C) Clearing Agency's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
NSCC has not received or solicited any written comments relating to this proposal. If any written comments are received by NSCC, they will be publicly filed as an Exhibit 2 to this filing, as required by Form 19b-4 and the General Instructions thereto.
Persons submitting comments are cautioned that, according to Section IV (Solicitation of Comments) of the Exhibit 1A in the General Instructions to Form 19b-4, the Commission does not edit personal identifying information from comment submissions. Commenters should submit only information that they wish to make available publicly, including their name, email address, and any other identifying information.
All prospective commenters should follow the Commission's instructions on how to submit comments,
available at
www.sec.gov/​rules-regulations/​how-submit-comment
.
General questions regarding the rule filing process or logistical questions regarding this filing should be directed to the Main Office of the Commission's Division of Trading and Markets at
tradingandmarkets@sec.gov
or 202-551-5777.
NSCC reserves the right not to respond to any comments received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change, and Timing for Commission Action
Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not:
(i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest;
(ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and
(iii) become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
25
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
26
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include File Number  SR-NSCC-2026-012 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549.
All submissions should refer to File Number SR-NSCC-2026-012. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of NSCC and on DTCC's website (
www.dtcc.com/​legal/​sec-rule-filings
). Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to File Number SR-NSCC-2026-012 and should be submitted on or before November 25, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
